transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 72 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Morgan (Redwood SE), Ivy Zhang (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Head of ML, Aperture), Carlos Ruiz (Platform), Evelyn Park (CTO)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark methodology, timeline and integration approach. Primary ask: validate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints + SDK integration for tool/function calling and structured JSON output for diagnostic report generation. Discussed dedicated vs hosted, VPC/private pilot, KPIs (p95 latency, throughput), and data residency/KMS needs.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria & acceptance tests
- Workload characterization (prompt sizes, concurrency)
- Benchmark plan + metrics (latency, cost, quality/regression checks)
- Integration approach: SDKs, OpenAI-compat endpoints, function-calling, structured output enforcement
- Deployment mode: hosted -> dedicated -> private (VPC) transition plan
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Timeline & next steps

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro round — we'll keep it focused on the POC scoping and integration playbook.
[00:08] Maya: Hi, thanks. Short intro from us — Aperture Diagnostics builds ML-first pipelines for near real-time image triage, and we're evaluating an LLM layer to produce structured diagnostic summaries and suggested next-steps for clinicians. Key constraints are P95 latency under 250ms for short prompts, and data never leaving our VPC for the private pilot.
[00:26] Carlos: Also want to be able to call our internal tooling via function-calling — like run a patient lookup or enqueue a case for specialist. So the function/tool calling path needs to be reliable and auditable.
[00:40] Leah: Great, that lines up with a lot of other healthcare pilots. To clarify — when you say structured diagnostic summaries, do you have a schema already? JSON fields, enumerations?
[00:50] Maya: Yes, we've sketched a schema — diagnosis_code, confidence_score, recommended_action [enum], and optional follow_up_items array. We'll share the draft. We need Redwood to enforce or validate structured output ideally so downstream consumers don't break.
[01:05] Samir: Perfect. For enforcement we can do two things in the POC: 1) use the OpenAI-compatible function-calling interface to return typed outputs; 2) run a small post-processor in the harness that validates and reports schema regressions. We'll include both in the benchmark.
[01:20] Evelyn: Can you give us an example benchmark? What do you measure beyond latency and cost?
[01:25] Leah: Sure — standard bench includes: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency spikes, tokens/sec throughput, concurrency behavior (N inflight requests), cold-start penalties for model variants, and output quality metrics — e.g., schema validity rate, F1 on labelled fields, and false positive rate for suggested actions. Also monitor KV cache hit rates where applicable, since prefix caching can dramatically reduce latency for repeated prompts.
[01:48] Carlos: How do you simulate real workload? Our prompts vary: short triage prompts (~30 tokens), medium case summaries (~200 tokens), and long case narratives (~800 tokens) with accompanying structured metadata.
[02:02] Leah: We'll ask you to provide representative prompt sets — at least 200 samples per class. Our harness will run them at 1x/5x/10x concurrency profiles to map latency curves. We'll also run an A/B against a baseline (your current OpenAI integration) if you want — that helps quantify cost/latency improvements.
[02:20] Maya: Yes, we'd like an apples-to-apples comparison versus our OpenAI usage.
[02:24] Samir: Noted. For the POC scope: two-week bench phase + one-week integration/bug-fix and then a canary for limited production. Timelinewise we're proposing 3 weeks total for the initial pilot. Does that align with your needs?
[02:36] Evelyn: That sounds reasonable. We'll need to lock success criteria though — our compliance team will require a list.
[02:42] Leah: Proposed success criteria (we'll iterate):
- Functional correctness: >= 98% schema-valid responses on the validation set
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms for short prompts, P95 <= 800ms for medium, and P95 <= 2.5s for long prompts (these are initial targets)
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime during bench windows, <0.5% error rate for function/tool calls
- Cost: token cost per request no worse than current OpenAI baseline by more than 15% when normalized for quality
- Security: VPC pilot with KMS wrapped keys + audit logs enabled for any PHI path

[03:15] Carlos: Curious about the OpenAI-compat endpoints — how close is the API surface? We have existing client code wrapping openai.Completion and ChatCompletion.
[03:25] Samir: Redwood offers an OpenAI-compatible endpoint layer — same REST routes and request shapes for chat/completions and function-calling. The SDKs support the same patterns and we also have a python client drop-in. You can re-point your clients. There are a few differences: extra fields for routing (e.g., capacity_tier), and model names are Redwood-specific. We'll share a migration guide.
[03:47] Maya: Are there subtle differences for function-calling signatures? We rely on parameter schemas and JSONSchema-like validation.
[03:54] Leah: We support schema-based function-calling; the runtime will try to return typed JSON and we have a schema validation step. For the pilot, we'll add a strict validation toggle so responses that don't conform get flagged and optionally routed to a fallback. Be aware that transcription may sometimes show as 'Redwood Dedicate' in logs, but underlying behavior is the same — little OCR hiccup.
[04:17] Evelyn: On deployment modes — we want to start hosted for speed, move to a dedicated pool for consistent latency, and then private VPC for production. How does that transition work operationally?
[04:29] Samir: We can do that. Typical path: hosted API access for early benching (no infra setup), then Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for the pilot to hit latency SLOs, and finally Redwood Private with VPC peering where the control plane is hosted but inference nodes are in your VPC or on-prem via a connector. Each step requires different lead times: hosted is immediate, dedicated provisioning is typically 2–3 weeks, private/VPC peering is 3–6 weeks depending on networking approvals.
[04:55] Carlos: For VPC, what do you need from our side?
[04:58] Leah: We'll need a service account, CIDR whitelist for peering, a service endpoint, and optionally an IAM role for KMS access. We'll provide a checklist and Terraform snippets.
[05:10] Maya: KMS — we need customer-managed keys for any PHI. Is HSM supported?
[05:14] Samir: Yes, KMS integrations and customer-managed keys are supported. For HSM-level controls we have partners and can discuss an enterprise add-on; we'll flag that for the EAP. For the POC, KMS with CMK is fine and audit logs will be turned on.
[05:28] Evelyn: Speaking of audits, do you capture token-level traces and prompt content in logs? We need redact/retention controls.
[05:33] Ivy: We can configure redaction and retention; by default hosted logs include token-level traces for debugging for admin users, but for clinical POCs we can turn off full prompt retention and keep only hashed digests and schema-level outputs. We'll include that configuration in the SOW.
[05:50] Carlos: Bench specifics — do you support continuous batching and KV caching? Our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes — patient meta, common preamble.
[05:58] Leah: The runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache. In the bench we'll measure cache hit rates and simulate prefix reuse so you can see unit token cost reductions. Note: logs sometimes show 'KV cash' in transcripts if auto-transcripted, ignore that.
[06:12] Maya: On quality metrics — can you run regression checks? We don't want model tuning to regress extraction quality.
[06:18] Leah: Yes, Redwood Optimize has a quality monitoring pipeline — tie evals to a golden prompt set and we'll alert on regression. For the POC we'll run nightly evals against your labelled set and notify if schema validity drops or F1 decreases by >2 points.
[06:34] Evelyn: How flexible is model selection? We may want to try multiple open models and an instruction-tuned variant.
[06:40] Samir: The catalog supports switching model variants. For the POC we'll pick 2-3 models (e.g., an instruction-tuned open model, a quantized low-latency variant, and your current baseline). We'll measure quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[06:52] Carlos: One more — can your function-calling trigger our job-queue with guaranteed once semantics? We use idempotent job APIs but need assurance.
[06:59] Leah: The function-calling path returns a structured payload to your webhook or to a Redwood-managed forwarder. For guaranteed semantics we'll recommend a lightweight acknowledgement pattern in your job API — the POC harness can stress test retries and duplicates and report the dedupe rate.
[07:15] Maya: Great. For acceptance, besides numbers, we need operational checks: ability to rotate keys, RBAC for the model endpoints, and audit trail for every model invocation.
[07:26] Ivy: We'll include RBAC mapping and logs. Key rotation is supported via KMS; rotation events are logged.
[07:31] Samir: To recap next steps: we'll send a POC SOW with three phases (bench 2 weeks, integration 1 week, canary limited rollout 1 week), pricing options (hosted vs reserved capacity), and a checklist for infra. Leah will share the benchmark harness and sample scripts. Maya/Carlos will provide the prompt sets and schema. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff during the week of 2026-01-26.
[07:53] Evelyn: Sounds good. One ask — can you include a small sample of the SDK migration steps for our python microservices?
[07:59] Leah: Yes, we'll attach a migration snippet and a quickstart repo link. Expect it by EOD 2026-01-22.
[08:07] Maya: Thanks, that helps. Also, please include a short checklist for security sign-off so our compliance team can start early.
[08:13] Samir: We'll add a compliance checklist and SOC2 artifacts link.
[08:16] Carlos: Anything else?
[08:18] Ivy: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and put the action items in the ticketing thread.
[08:23] Samir: Great — thanks all. We'll loop back once the SOW and harness are shared.

End of transcript.
